title: How do you deal with the slop?
author: AnxiousIntender
selftext:
I'm trying to get AI to generate unique game mechanics and content without babysitting every output. But when I ask for something unique, I get something that's mediocre. I tried changing sampling parameters, providers, models and nothing helps. I tried asking it to follow creativity frameworks and it barely did anything.  
  
Is this just how it works or has anyone actually cracked this? I'm frustrated to see everyone post cool projects but everything I make is just slop unless I supervise every step, which is unfeasible for what I'm trying to achieve.

comments.author: RUSuper
comments.body:
You are asking AI to invent you something unique? Or you have an idea in your head what you want exactly and ask it for it? 

Not sure I quite understand what your process here is? Sounds to me like you ask of AI to do everything of you, including coming up with ideas.

replies.author: AnxiousIntender
replies.body: I have the design. I'm asking it to execute my design, but the output still comes out generic/mediocre even when I specify exactly what I want. It's only good when I give it a screen recording and ask it to replicate the reference.

replies.author: AnxiousIntender
replies.body: I gave it one mechanic, "things stop when you look at them", and ran several creativity techniques on it (SCAMPER, bisociation, etc.) and blind reviewed all of them. Several were just reskins of Slender-man and SCP-173. Only 1 scored above 7 (out of 10). The rest felt familiar and not actually fun.

replies.author: RUSuper
replies.body:
I don't get it, why not just write simple sentence and not run bunch of overly complex skills that serve nothing good in this particular case? What is the to score in mechanic such as this? 

Also scores of "harsh critic" or whatever the hell is pointless, that critic is still an AI. You need to score them yourself by eye. If you don't like the look of behaviour of something then you tweak and redo it. You don't accept thing being "good" just because AI said it's good.

replies.author: Hot_Professional8287
replies.body:
I'm so confused. "things stop when you look at them" is a crude prompt for.. presumably AI behavior of a creature/entity, but then you're discussing reskins (a reference to a generated asset.. from a behavior prompt?).. and then there's a scoring system (whose? yours? on what basis?) in which 1 registers as >7.

What the hell is going on here lol

comments.author: QueenSavara
comments.body:
You deal with the slop with not letting AI design stuff but execute your designs. What you're doing is what gives everyone slop. 

Get your hands dirty to get good results, be lazy get slop.

comments.author: 2eggs1stone
comments.body: There's no such thing as free lunch.  Creativity is doing the thing that no one else is creating.  There are better things to optimize for than creativity.  Put your own blood and sweat into the project and let the LLM allow you to implement that faster.  If you're not creative, there's nothing wrong with that, but expect to make generic slop because that's what you'll get.  Now don't get me wrong, no one is creative in every way, some parts of your product are going to be generic and average, but there should be something that you bring to the table that makes your product uniquely you.

comments.author: Every-Prize4720
comments.body: broh

comments.author: Zealousideal-Bar-316
comments.body:
That’s the thing: the mechanics and the game shouldn't be created by them—they should only provide development support; the idea has to be yours. I’ve been gaming since I was eight years old—I’m 34 now and never stopped—and I have thousands of different game ideas thanks to my experience as a player.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/5181900/Runecast\_Demo/

This is a game of mine—a simple autobattler. I'm finishing up a major update that improves the graphics and adds a new mechanic. AI isn't creative, always remember that.

comments.author: AlgaeNo3373
comments.body:
The babysitting part is the gamedev part tbh. It's minutiae and fiddly shit that an LLM will not intuit well. 

So yeah imo, just how it work, even without AI!  
  
Note that asking for something "unique" is kinda brutal to an LLM. They respond based on probability. They're as original as a contestant's answer on Family Fued and scored/rewarded the same way. Like broadly speaking originality is not something reinforced, but predictability is. They do their best work closest to the distribution - i.e. unoriginality is their bread and butter. In some technical/philosophical ways, people argue they're literally *incapable* of unique/original because they're just remixing known things.

I'm currently on the 5000th iteration of my UI and I have pics of Makita drills open, ruggedized tough shit. That's the current concept. It's not something an LLM would've reached for without me in the loop yanking the steering wheel. That's kinda your job in all this imvho and something where the human creativity can still shine, so why try to automate it away anyhow?! <3

comments.author: Suspicious_Bird8950
comments.body: LLM will not create anything unique. It takes other ppl ideas and creations and create paste from and then feeds it to the end user. Go with 'hey i have this idea ... who is doing anything like this or similiar?' and go on from there.

comments.author: Ulnari
comments.body: I don't believe AI can offer genuine ideas and unique game mechanics. It can help you refine your ideas though.

comments.author: Affectionate_Fact854
comments.body:
This is the problem,  you can't expect ai to implement and create mechanics out of thin air and expect them to be good 


Ai won't take away manual itteration and human testing 
And ai doesn't know what makes a mechanic fun 

Unless you tell it to just simply clone another game, you will need to be clear on the idea and goals

comments.author: Big_Presentation2786
comments.body: I tell AI what I want, I tell it how to do it, I don't put up with a standard it thinks is okay, if I feel it's not representative of my quality

comments.author: monsterfurby
comments.body: One thing I learned is that GenAI is good at realizing a plan. It is, however, even better at creating a *facsimile of a plan* that will turn out to be terrible once put into reality. You don't need to babysit the details of technical development, but you absolutely should take the time to detail out your concept.

comments.author: caxco93
comments.body: break it down into actionable steps

comments.author: DoctorBrandonLau
comments.body:
What are you trying to make? Personally I think using one shot prompts is a bad way to make games. 

I personally start with a simple character on either a 3d or 2d map with the very basic mechanics and gameplay and then add more mechanics and elements iteratively being very specific each time. Full locations, Maps and story come after.

All solo game projects from developers that don’t use AI start this way and I strongly believe it is still the best way to do things regardless of whether you use AI or not.

comments.author: Ichiban_dev
comments.body: Prime example of a dumbass finally having access to some form of intelligence for the first time and not knowing what to do with it.

comments.author: TheReviewerWildTake
comments.body:
AI is anything but uniqueness. The nature of neural networks is that in order to produce something decent, it has to have references. The more the better.   
  
And only generic, mundane, mass-produced things have a lot of references.  
The moment you want unique thing - the amount of references plummets.  
  
This is why AI is so good at doing fundamentals, but is progressively worse as you go into truly unique context of specific project.

You have to babysit it at that and learn the craft, to be able to isolate AI tasks at things that it is able to do, and then do other parts yourself.

comments.author: pickleunicorn
comments.body: I'm a professional developer who uses AI everyday for several months and the thing is : you need to drive AI with small steps. Try to make it generate everything all at once and you will get only slop.

comments.author: YKLKTMA
comments.body:
AI doesn’t generate anything truly unique by the nature of how LLMs work. In fact, it isn’t really intelligence at all.

AI is a tool that amplifies human ability, not a magic “make something great for me, quickly” button.

The less the person using the LLM knows, the less skill they have, and the less effort they put in, the worse the output will be.

comments.author: soulglider26
comments.body:
Rofl.

"AI please make me money! and cool game! hmm this doesn't work"

Are you.. serious or is this a troll?

replies.author: AnxiousIntender
replies.body: I'm just trying to see if there's any way to accelerate the progress :/

comments.author: F1ak3r
comments.body: You have to babysit every output. AI can speed up a lot of things but a human being still has to care about the details in the final product. I don't think this will change for creative work, no matter how good the models get.

comments.author: Inner-Core-Studios
comments.body: So you dont want to code, make game art, level design etc yourself. Sure. But you dont even want to steer where your game is going? Maybe this isnt for you.

comments.author: SilliCarl
comments.body: Generally when I use AI I have a very distinct and solid image of the thing that I want to create. AI isn't there to do my thinking for me, its there to implement the ideas that I already came up with. I look at it more like being the lead design on a game where I have employees under me who will do the actual "make this idea work" part.

comments.author: Altruistic-Spare9069
comments.body: You dont need babysit if you have a good harness but you need to give him ideas , as he doesnt think like human and his ideas are not so funny. You need to act as game designer and give him tasks , review them visually and play the game to get the feeling , rinse and repeat . He can code it for you or solve technical issues but you can't tell him "make this better, invent cool mechanic , make the wow effect" , those things rarely work , dont trust the videos of one prompt games, thats bullshit

comments.author: nokafein
comments.body:
Okay repeat after me: AI CAN’T CREATE NEW THINGS. 

You must be the game dev, plan, think, invent, come up with ideas. Ai is there to help you fasten the process, not replace these things for you.

comments.author: hunteel
comments.body: If you don't know what you want AI can't imagine for you, so it uses what they programmed to be the standard and that's the slop.

comments.author: LazyAp3
comments.body: Honestly not knowing what you use and how means nobody here can help you in any decent way but my generic advice for most AI generation is 1. Good Agent 2. References for good guidance 3. A good prompt 4. Small scope tasks 5. Human touch for the finish helps tremendously
